sections.overview: The Mangrove Cuckoo is a secretive tropical American cuckoo; unlike forest-edge C. erythropthalmus, it often uses coastal scrub.
sections.identification: Its long tail, brown upperparts, barred underside and partly yellow lower bill distinguish it.
sections.habitat: It uses mangroves, beach scrub and tropical woodland, with habitat varying across its broad Caribbean and mainland range.
sections.diet: It takes insects, spiders, frogs, lizards, eggs, nestlings and fruit, often foraging in the canopy.
sections.behavior: Both parents build the nest, incubate and feed the young.
sections.reproduction: The nest is a loose twig platform placed in a tree, often close to or over water.
sections.ecology: In Florida, its habitat includes mangrove forest and tropical hardwood hammock.
sections.conservation: Cornell reports declines in Florida that are probably linked to habitat loss and fragmentation.
